attempts.summary: Established an AIDE-based file integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (RHEL 9): installed aide, confirmed the default /etc/aide.conf already covers all of /etc (explicit per-path rules plus a catch-all `/etc PERMS`), initialized the database (39,334 entries), activated it as /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz, recorded its SHA256 and an establishment timestamp, and validated detection by injecting test files under /etc (AIDE reported 2 added entries) then cleaning them up and reconfirming a clean check. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id/btime and a clean aide check, issued `systemctl reboot`, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed (377b5195... -> 7e980b46...) and uptime reset, then verified the aide database file and its SHA256 were unchanged and a post-restart `aide --check` still reported no differences, proving the baseline survived the restart.
